content:
incidents-bot: P1 ALERT — Control plane dependency failures. Elevated 5xx across auth/org-lookup paths since ~09:02 UTC. Impact: token exchanges and org lookup calls returning 502/504; some downstream gateways seeing cascading 5xx. Pagerduty: PD#INC-2026-345 created. Please ack. :rotating_light:

alice_oncall: acked. I’m on it. paging ben.

ben_sre: looking... grabbing graphs (Grafana link: https://grafana.company.internal/d/ctrlplane/ctrlplane-deps). seeing spike in 5xx on /v1/auth/exchange and /v1/org/lookup at 09:01 — error rate ~11% in last 5m. Latency also up to 1.2s p95.

dave_runtime: any recent deploys to control-plane-auth?

deploy-bot: deploy:controlplane-auth v3.14.2 -> v3.14.3 completed rolling update at 08:58 UTC (deploy-id: dpl-89012).

ben_sre: ok deploy correlates. Quick check of pods: `kubectl -n controlplane get pods -l app=cp-auth` shows many restarts on node gpu-14. `kubectl logs cp-auth-7f6d -c cp-auth` shows repeated `org-lookup timeout: dial tcp 10.20.30.40:443: i/o timeout` and `upstream returned 502` errors.

frank_prod: customers reporting token failures via support. Erica, can you triage severity?

erica_support: initial triage: about ~25% of recent support tickets mention login errors or 502 on API calls. High-touch customers flagged (acct: acme-corp, star-platform). Velocity spike on support queue.

alice_oncall: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) roll back v3.14.3 if deploy caused regression, 2) enable fallback cache for org-lookup to reduce dependency calls, 3) increase retry budget + circuit-breaker on gateway. Ben — can you triage whether rollback is safe?

ben_sre: rolling back is option. But first quick mitigation: enable read-through cache on org-lookup service and flip auth to use cached tokens for 10m TTL to reduce load. I have a config flag in config service `feature.org_lookup_cache=true` we can flip. Pushing change to config store now.

carla_platform: I can flip the config and do a canary. Will push to config-store and then to control plane config.

carla_platform: (runs) `curl -XPOST https://config.internal/api/flags -d '{"key":"org_lookup_cache","value":true}'` — response 200. Pushing target rollouts to control-plane-config.

carla_platform: pushed change and bumped rollout to 10% of auth nodes. Observability: org-lookup calls dropping by ~40% on canary pods.

ben_sre: good. also enable gateway circuit-breaker to fail fast on org-lookup path. `kubectl apply -f gateway-cb.yaml` where cb limit lowered to 5 concurrent and fast-fail. Doing it now.

ben_sre: applied. early signs: total request errors dropping from 11% -> 6% on canary region.

alice_oncall: frank, customer comms — ask affected accounts to retry and note we’re mitigating; mark as degraded with ETA 30m.

frank_prod: on it. Sending note via statuspage draft: "Degraded performance for authentication and org lookups, intermittent 5xx. Engineers are mitigating. ETA 30m."

dave_runtime: investigating node gps/host network issues — node gpu-14 shows kernel logs with high tcp retransmits. Might be infra-level network flakiness causing org-lookup timeouts to the external org service. Not purely app.

ben_sre: interesting — if network flakiness, rollback might not fully resolve. Suggest take two-pronged approach: keep cache + cb + transient rollback if we still see errors after fixes.

alice_oncall: agree. Ben, can you create short runbook steps for on-call to follow if errors persist? Put in this thread.

ben_sre: runbook snippet: 1) Check Grafana for auth/org-lookup error rate, 2) Verify config flag `org_lookup_cache` in config-store, 3) Check `kubectl get pods -n controlplane -l app=cp-auth` for restarts, 4) If >30% nodes show network errors, open infra ticket and move traffic away from affected AZ, 5) Rollback auth deploy `kubectl rollout undo deployment/cp-auth --to-revision=3` if after 20m cache+CB don’t steady.

dave_runtime: moving traffic off node gpu-14 by cordoning and draining: `kubectl cordon gpu-14 && kubectl drain gpu-14 --ignore-daemonsets --force` — starting now.

ben_sre: after drain, auth pod restarts redistributed. Error rate improving further — now ~3% 5xx across control plane. p95 latency back down to 350ms.

alice_oncall: great. Keep monitoring for 30m. If stable, we’ll close PD and move to postmortem. Carol/Carla, are there any config rollbacks to keep?

carla_platform: we left `org_lookup_cache=true` enabled on 100% after canary because it helped. Will file a follow-up change to tune TTLs and monitor hit/miss ratio.

erica_support: updating status page: added note that mitigation applied and we’re seeing improvement; asked customers to reach out if they still see errors.

frank_prod: sending targeted DM to acme-corp and star-platform with update and ask to retry auth.

alice_oncall: PD#INC-2026-345 — assigning on-call handoff to carla for next shift. I’ll remain in thread for runbook capture. Handoff: pagerduty:carla.

carla_platform: acked. I’m the new owner. Monitoring windows: 30m. Will escalate to infra if reappearance.

deploy-bot: rollback option ready: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/cp-auth --to-revision=3` (safe window until 10:30 UTC).

ben_sre: logs and artifacts for postmortem: saved pod logs to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-345/logs.tar.gz; saved grafana snapshots.

alice_oncall: summary for incident record (copy to ticket): - root cause: combination of recent deploy (v3.14.3) and transient host-level network issues causing org-lookup timeouts; - impact: auth/org-lookup 5xx spike ~09:01–09:20 UTC, peak ~11% errors, affected hosted API and some customers; - mitigation: enable org lookup cache, applied gateway circuit-breaker, cordoned problematic node and drained pods, then scaled stable pods; - status: resolved/mitigated, currently 3% error rate and falling; owner: carla_platform for follow-up.

erica_support: ticket updated, customers notified.

carla_platform: I will open a postmortem and include suggestions: deploy gating for network-sensitive changes, add host-level network health check gating, and automated fallback cache for org lookups.

alice_oncall: closing notes: leaving PD in acknowledgement state until tomorrow handoff. If it flares again, re-open PD and re-escalate. Great work team. :tada:
